title: Homogeneous fraction charts for an individual Proj twist
statement: Let A be a commutative N-graded ring with grading 𝒜. For every integer k, the locally-fraction sheaf twist 𝒜 k [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] admits compatible additive charts beta on every D₊(f), f homogeneous of positive degree. The chart is injective into LocalizedModule.Away f A, with range degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] for the shifted grading: y has degree n when y lies in 𝒜_(k+n) if k+n is nonnegative, and is zero otherwise. It intertwines awayToSection scalars with the homogeneous-localization algebra map. If D₊(g) is contained in D₊(f) and g^e=h*f with e>0 and h homogeneous, restriction carries y/f^m to h^m*y/g^(e*m). No nonnilpotence or restriction on k is assumed.

source.place: Definition 27.10.1 (1), Tag 01MN; Lemma 27.8.4 (2),(3), Tag 01M7, applied to A(k)

proof.text: Apply the degree-k fraction construction pointwise at homogeneous primes. Fractions with a denominator f^m define locally-fraction sections on D₊(f). Their equivalence relation is preserved under localization at every point. Conversely cover a locally-fraction section by basic opens on which it has a homogeneous fraction representative. D₊(f) is affine for homogeneous f of positive degree, hence a finite subcover suffices. Clearing the finitely many denominators and overlap equality witnesses yields a homogeneous representative y/f^m of degree k. The same finite-cover argument applied to a zero section proves injectivity of the map from these fractions into sections. Invert that bijection to obtain beta. Its range in the ordinary localized module is precisely the equal-degree fractions of the shift A(k), by the definition of degreeZeroFractions. Negative graded components of A are zero. When f is nilpotent, both the sections on the empty open and the localization are zero.

Pointwise multiplication of fractions gives scalar compatibility. For g^e=h*f, the element h/g^e in A_g is an inverse of f. The localization homomorphism therefore carries y/f^m to h^m*y/g^(e*m). Evaluating both expressions at every homogeneous prime of D₊(g) proves that this agrees with restriction of the locally-fraction sections.

proof_origin.place: Definition 27.10.1 (1), Tag 01MN; Lemma 27.8.4 (2),(3), Tag 01M7, applied to A(k); adaptation to the locally-fraction twist and finite coordinate interfaces

theorem single_twist_basicOpen_fractions
    {A σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] :
    ∃ beta : ∀ (k : ℤ) (f : A) (b : ℕ), 0 < b → f ∈ 𝒜 b →
      (twist 𝒜 k).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f)) →+ LocalizedModule.Away f A,
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b),
      Function.Injective (beta k f b hb hf) ∧
      Set.range (beta k f b hb hf) = degreeZeroFractions
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set A))
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ {y : A | if 0 ≤ k + n then y ∈ 𝒜 (k + n).toNat else y = 0})
        (Submonoid.powers f)) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b)
      (q : HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
      (s : (twist 𝒜 k).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
      beta k f b hb hf (awayToSection 𝒜 f q • s) =
        algebraMap (HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f) (Localization.Away f) q •
          beta k f b hb hf s) ∧
    (∀ (k : ℤ) (f g : A) (b c : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c)
      (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b) (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 c) (inc : basicOpen 𝒜 g ≤ basicOpen 𝒜 f)
      (e t : ℕ) (h : A), 0 < e → h ∈ 𝒜 t → g ^ e = h * f →
      ∀ (m : ℕ) (y : A) (s : (twist 𝒜 k).val.obj (op (basicOpen 𝒜 f))),
        beta k f b hb hf s = mk y (⟨f ^ m, ⟨m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers f) →
        beta k g c hc hg ((twist 𝒜 k).val.map (homOfLE inc).op s) =
          mk (h ^ m • y)
            (⟨g ^ (e * m), ⟨e * m, rfl⟩⟩ : Submonoid.powers g))
